relationships.subject: suzetrigine
relationships.evidence_quote: Suzetrigine exerts its analgesic effect by selectively blocking NaV1.8 on peripheral nociceptors, specifically in primary dorsal root ganglion neurons, thereby preventing pain signal transduction.17

relationships.subject: CYP3A4
relationships.evidence_quote: Suzetrigine is extensively metabolized in the liver by CYP3A4 to an active metabolite, and both the parent compound and its metabolite are ultimately excreted in feces and urine.12,17

relationships.subject: suzetrigine
relationships.evidence_quote: Because suzetrigine is a CYP3A4 substrate and inducer, its use may be limited in those with drug or food interactions.

key_findings: Suzetrigine blocks NaV1.8 on peripheral nociceptors and produced meaningful 48-hour pain reductions versus placebo in phase 3 trials, without superiority over hydrocodone/acetaminophen.
Suzetrigine is a CYP3A4 substrate and inducer, creating interaction risks; use beyond 14 days is unstudied.
